questions.question: Describe where and how gold is mined in South Africa.
questions.expected_answer: Gold is mined in the Witwatersrand Basin, under parts of Gauteng, the Free State and North West, where it was found in 1886. It is in thin, sloping layers of rock called reefs, deep underground, and some mines are more than three kilometres deep. Miners drill and blast the rock, and the ore is lifted to the surface. Most ore contains only a few grams of gold per tonne.

questions.question: Explain how gold ore is turned into a gold bar.
questions.expected_answer: The ore is crushed and ground into fine powder at a processing plant. Chemicals dissolve the gold out of the powder, and the gold is collected again. It is melted in a furnace and poured into bars, which are sent to a refinery, such as the Rand Refinery in Germiston, where other metals are removed until the gold is almost pure.

questions.question: Explain how a jeweller adds value to gold, and what carats tell us.
questions.expected_answer: The jeweller mixes gold with other metals to make a harder alloy, designs the piece, melts and casts the gold, rolls it or draws it into wire, shapes and joins it, adds stones and polishes it. The design, skill, time and tools add value, so the jewellery is worth more than the gold in it. Carats show how much gold is in the alloy: twenty-four carat is almost pure, eighteen carat is about three-quarters gold and nine carat a little more than one-third.
